body_params.name: state
body_params.description: Requested resource state.
body_params.verbose_description:
Requested resource state. The CRM reads this state and acts accordingly.
Please note that `enabled` is just an alias for `started`.

`started`;;

The CRM tries to start the resource. Service state is
set to `started` after successful start. On node failures, or when start
fails, it tries to recover the resource.  If everything fails, service
state it set to `error`.

`stopped`;;

The CRM tries to keep the resource in `stopped` state, but it
still tries to relocate the resources on node failures.

`disabled`;;

The CRM tries to put the resource in `stopped` state, but does not try
to relocate the resources on node failures. The main purpose of this
state is error recovery, because it is the only way to move a resource out
of the `error` state.

`ignored`;;

The resource gets removed from the manager status and so the CRM and the LRM do
not touch the resource anymore. All {pve} API calls affecting this resource
will be executed, directly bypassing the HA stack. CRM commands will be thrown
away while there source is in this state. The resource will not get relocated
on node failures.

The CRM tries to put the resource in `stopped` state, but does not try
to relocate the resources on node failures. The main purpose of this
state is error recovery, because it is the only way to move a resource out
of the `error` state.

`ignored`;;

The resource gets removed from the manager status and so the CRM and the LRM do
not touch the resource anymore. All {pve} API calls affecting this resource
will be executed, directly bypassing the HA stack. CRM commands will be thrown
away while there source is in this state. The resource will not get relocated
on node failures.

body_params.verbose_description:
Create a serial device inside the VM (n is 0 to 3), and pass through a
host serial device (i.e. /dev/ttyS0), or create a unix socket on the
host side (use 'qm terminal' to open a terminal connection).

body_params.description: Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd.

body_params.verbose_description: Enable/disable the USB tablet device. This device is usually needed to allow absolute mouse positioning with VNC. Else the mouse runs out of sync with normal VNC clients. If you're running lots of console-only guests on one host, you may consider disabling this to save some context switches. This is turned off by default if you use spice (-vga=qxl).

The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

body_params.verbose_description:
Configure the VGA Hardware. If you want to use high resolution modes (>= 1280x1024x16) you may need to increase the vga memory option. Since QEMU 2.9 the default VGA display type is 'std' for all OS types besides some Windows versions (XP and older) which use 'cirrus'. The 'qxl' option enables the SPICE display server. For win* OS you can select how many independent displays you want, Linux guests can add displays them self.
You can also run without any graphic card, using a serial device as terminal.

body_params.verbose_description:
The VM generation ID (vmgenid) device exposes a 128-bit integer value identifier to the guest OS. This allows to notify the guest operating system when the virtual machine is executed with a different configuration (e.g. snapshot execution or creation from a template). The guest operating system notices the change, and is then able to react as appropriate by marking its copies of distributed databases as dirty, re-initializing its random number generator, etc.
Note that auto-creation only works when done throug API/CLI create or update methods, but not when manually editing the config file.

is called 'vmbr0'.

The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

usb3.description: Specifies whether if given host option is a USB3 device or port (this does currently not work reliably with spice redirection and is then ignored).

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

ipconfig[n].description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using dhcp on IPv4.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

vga.verbose_description:
Configure the VGA Hardware. If you want to use high resolution modes (>= 1280x1024x16) you may need to increase the vga memory option. Since QEMU 2.9 the default VGA display type is 'std' for all OS types besides some Windows versions (XP and older) which use 'cirrus'. The 'qxl' option enables the SPICE display server. For win* OS you can select how many independent displays you want, Linux guests can add displays them self.
You can also run without any graphic card, using a serial device as terminal.

vmgenid.verbose_description:
The VM generation ID (vmgenid) device exposes a 128-bit integer value identifier to the guest OS. This allows to notify the guest operating system when the virtual machine is executed with a different configuration (e.g. snapshot execution or creation from a template). The guest operating system notices the change, and is then able to react as appropriate by marking its copies of distributed databases as dirty, re-initializing its random number generator, etc.
Note that auto-creation only works when done throug API/CLI create or update methods, but not when manually editing the config file.

body_params.name: ipconfig[n]
body_params.description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using dhcp on IPv4.

body_params.name: ivshmem
body_params.description: Inter-VM shared memory. Useful for direct communication between VMs, or to the host.

name.description: The name of the file. Will be prefixed with 'pve-shm-'. Default is the VMID. Will be deleted when the VM is stopped.

size.description: The size of the file in MB.

body_params.name: keyboard
body_params.description: Keybord layout for vnc server. Default is read from the '/etc/pve/datacenter.cfg' configuration file.It should not be necessary to set it.

body_params.name: kvm
body_params.description: Enable/disable KVM hardware virtualization.

body_params.name: localtime
body_params.description: Set the real time clock to local time. This is enabled by default if ostype indicates a Microsoft OS.

body_params.name: lock
body_params.description: Lock/unlock the VM.

body_params.name: machine
body_params.description: Specifies the Qemu machine type.

body_params.name: memory
body_params.description: Amount of RAM for the VM in MB. This is the maximum available memory when you use the balloon device.

body_params.name: migrate_downtime
body_params.description: Set maximum tolerated downtime (in seconds) for migrations.

body_params.name: migrate_speed
body_params.description: Set maximum speed (in MB/s) for migrations. Value 0 is no limit.

body_params.name: name
body_params.description: Set a name for the VM. Only used on the configuration web interface.

body_params.name: nameserver
body_params.description: cloud-init: Sets DNS server IP address for a container. Create will automatically use the setting from the host if neither searchdomain nor nameserver are set.

body_params.name: net[n]
body_params.description: Specify network devices.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.
macaddr.verbose_description: A common MAC address with the I/G (Individual/Group) bit not set.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

body_params.name: numa
body_params.description: Enable/disable NUMA.

body_params.name: numa[n]
body_params.description: NUMA topology.

memory.description: Amount of memory this NUMA node provides.

body_params.name: onboot
body_params.description: Specifies whether a VM will be started during system bootup.

body_params.name: ostype
body_params.description: Specify guest operating system.
body_params.verbose_description:
Specify guest operating system. This is used to enable special
optimization/features for specific operating systems:

[horizontal]
other;; unspecified OS
wxp;; Microsoft Windows XP
w2k;; Microsoft Windows 2000
w2k3;; Microsoft Windows 2003
w2k8;; Microsoft Windows 2008
wvista;; Microsoft Windows Vista
win7;; Microsoft Windows 7
win8;; Microsoft Windows 8/2012/2012r2
win10;; Microsoft Windows 10/2016
l24;; Linux 2.4 Kernel
l26;; Linux 2.6/3.X Kernel
solaris;; Solaris/OpenSolaris/OpenIndiania kernel

body_params.verbose_description:

host serial device (i.e. /dev/ttyS0), or create a unix socket on the
host side (use 'qm terminal' to open a terminal connection).

NOTE: If you pass through a host serial device, it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

CAUTION: Experimental! User reported problems with this option.

body_params.name: shares
body_params.description: Amount of memory shares for auto-ballooning. The larger the number is, the more memory this VM gets. Number is relative to weights of all other running VMs. Using zero disables auto-ballooning. Auto-ballooning is done by pvestatd.

body_params.name: startdate
body_params.description: Set the initial date of the real time clock. Valid format for date are: 'now' or '2006-06-17T16:01:21' or '2006-06-17'.

body_params.name: startup
body_params.description: Startup and shutdown behavior. Order is a non-negative number defining the general startup order. Shutdown in done with reverse ordering. Additionally you can set the 'up' or 'down' delay in seconds, which specifies a delay to wait before the next VM is started or stopped.

body_params.name: tablet
body_params.description: Enable/disable the USB tablet device.
body_params.verbose_description: Enable/disable the USB tablet device. This device is usually needed to allow absolute mouse positioning with VNC. Else the mouse runs out of sync with normal VNC clients. If you're running lots of console-only guests on one host, you may consider disabling this to save some context switches. This is turned off by default if you use spice (-vga=qxl).

body_params.name: tdf
body_params.description: Enable/disable time drift fix.

body_params.name: template
body_params.description: Enable/disable Template.

body_params.name: unused[n]

body_params.name: usb[n]
body_params.description: Configure an USB device (n is 0 to 4).

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

usb3.description: Specifies whether if given host option is a USB3 device or port (this does currently not work reliably with spice redirection and is then ignored).

body_params.name: vcpus
body_params.description: Number of hotplugged vcpus.

body_params.name: vga
body_params.description: Configure the VGA hardware.

memory.description: Sets the VGA memory (in MiB). Has no effect with serial display.

body_params.verbose_description:
Configure the VGA Hardware. If you want to use high resolution modes (>= 1280x1024x16) you may need to increase the vga memory option. Since QEMU 2.9 the default VGA display type is 'std' for all OS types besides some Windows versions (XP and older) which use 'cirrus'. The 'qxl' option enables the SPICE display server. For win* OS you can select how many independent displays you want, Linux guests can add displays them self.
You can also run without any graphic card, using a serial device as terminal.

body_params.description: Set VM Generation ID. Use '1' to autogenerate on create or update, pass '0' to disable explicitly.
body_params.verbose_description:
The VM generation ID (vmgenid) device exposes a 128-bit integer value identifier to the guest OS. This allows to notify the guest operating system when the virtual machine is executed with a different configuration (e.g. snapshot execution or creation from a template). The guest operating system notices the change, and is then able to react as appropriate by marking its copies of distributed databases as dirty, re-initializing its random number generator, etc.
Note that auto-creation only works when done throug API/CLI create or update methods, but not when manually editing the config file.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

body_params.description:
cloud-init: Specify IP addresses and gateways for the corresponding interface.

IP addresses use CIDR notation, gateways are optional but need an IP of the same type specified.

The special string 'dhcp' can be used for IP addresses to use DHCP, in which case no explicit gateway should be provided.
For IPv6 the special string 'auto' can be used to use stateless autoconfiguration.

If cloud-init is enabled and neither an IPv4 nor an IPv6 address is specified, it defaults to using dhcp on IPv4.

body_params.description: Specify network devices.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.
macaddr.verbose_description: A common MAC address with the I/G (Individual/Group) bit not set.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

Since QEMU 2.9 the default VGA display type is 'std' for all OS types besides some Windows versions (XP and older) which use 'cirrus'. The 'qxl' option enables the SPICE display server. For win* OS you can select how many independent displays you want, Linux guests can add displays them self.
You can also run without any graphic card, using a serial device as terminal.

body_params.verbose_description:
The VM generation ID (vmgenid) device exposes a 128-bit integer value identifier to the guest OS. This allows to notify the guest operating system when the virtual machine is executed with a different configuration (e.g. snapshot execution or creation from a template). The guest operating system notices the change, and is then able to react as appropriate by marking its copies of distributed databases as dirty, re-initializing its random number generator, etc.
Note that auto-creation only works when done throug API/CLI create or update methods, but not when manually editing the config file.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

host.description:
The Host USB device or port or the value 'spice'. HOSTUSBDEVICE syntax is:

 'bus-port(.port)*' (decimal numbers) or
 'vendor_id:product_id' (hexadeciaml numbers) or
 'spice'

You can use the 'lsusb -t' command to list existing usb devices.

NOTE: This option allows direct access to host hardware. So it is no longer possible to migrate such machines - use with special care.

The value 'spice' can be used to add a usb redirection devices for spice.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

bridge.description:
Bridge to attach the network device to. The Proxmox VE standard bridge
is called 'vmbr0'.

If you do not specify a bridge, we create a kvm user (NATed) network
device, which provides DHCP and DNS services. The following addresses
are used:

 10.0.2.2   Gateway
 10.0.2.3   DNS Server
 10.0.2.4   SMB Server

The DHCP server assign addresses to the guest starting from 10.0.2.15.

firewall.description: Whether this interface should be protected by the firewall.

link_down.description: Whether this interface should be disconnected (like pulling the plug).

macaddr.description: MAC address. That address must be unique withing your network. This is automatically generated if not specified.

model.description: Network Card Model. The 'virtio' model provides the best performance with very low CPU overhead. If your guest does not support this driver, it is usually best to use 'e1000'.

queues.description: Number of packet queues to be used on the device.

rate.description: Rate limit in mbps (megabytes per second) as floating point number.

tag.description: VLAN tag to apply to packets on this interface.

trunks.description: VLAN trunks to pass through this interface.

body_params.description:

fuse.description: Allow using 'fuse' file systems in a container. Note that interactions between fuse and the freezer cgroup can potentially cause I/O deadlocks.

keyctl.description: For unprivileged containers only: Allow the use of the keyctl() system call. This is required to use docker inside a container. By default unprivileged containers will see this system call as non-existent. This is mostly a workaround for systemd-networkd, as it will treat it as a fatal error when some keyctl() operations are denied by the kernel due to lacking permissions. Essentially, you can choose between running systemd-networkd or docker.

mount.description: Allow mounting file systems of specific types. This should be a list of file system types as used with the mount command. Note that this can have negative effects on the container's security. With access to a loop device, mounting a file can circumvent the mknod permission of the devices cgroup, mounting an NFS file system can block the host's I/O completely and prevent it from rebooting, etc.

nesting.description: Allow nesting. Best used with unprivileged containers with additional id mapping. Note that this will expose procfs and sysfs contents of the host to the guest.

keyctl.description: For unprivileged containers only: Allow the use of the keyctl() system call. This is required to use docker inside a container. By default unprivileged containers will see this system call as non-existent. This is mostly a workaround for systemd-networkd, as it will treat it as a fatal error when some keyctl() operations are denied by the kernel due to lacking permissions. Essentially, you can choose between running systemd-networkd or docker.

mount.description: Allow mounting file systems of specific types. This should be a list of file system types as used with the mount command. Note that this can have negative effects on the container's security. With access to a loop device, mounting a file can circumvent the mknod permission of the devices cgroup, mounting an NFS file system can block the host's I/O completely and prevent it from rebooting, etc.

nesting.description: Allow nesting. Best used with unprivileged containers with additional id mapping. Note that this will expose procfs and sysfs contents of the host to the guest.

fuse.description: Allow using 'fuse' file systems in a container. Note that interactions between fuse and the freezer cgroup can potentially cause I/O deadlocks.

cmode.description: Console mode. By default, the console command tries to open a connection to one of the available tty devices. By setting cmode to 'console' it tries to attach to /dev/console instead. If you set cmode to 'shell', it simply invokes a shell inside the container (no login).

console.description: Attach a console device (/dev/console) to the container.

cores.description: The number of cores assigned to the container. A container can use all available cores by default.

cpulimit.description:
Limit of CPU usage.

NOTE: If the computer has 2 CPUs, it has a total of '2' CPU time. Value '0' indicates no CPU limit.

cpuunits.description:
CPU weight for a VM. Argument is used in the kernel fair scheduler. The larger the number is, the more CPU time this VM gets. Number is relative to the weights of all the other running VMs.

NOTE: You can disable fair-scheduler configuration by setting this to 0.

keyctl.description: For unprivileged containers only: Allow the use of the keyctl() system call. This is required to use docker inside a container. By default unprivileged containers will see this system call as non-existent. This is mostly a workaround for systemd-networkd, as it will treat it as a fatal error when some keyctl() operations are denied by the kernel due to lacking permissions. Essentially, you can choose between running systemd-networkd or docker.

mount.description: Allow mounting file systems of specific types. This should be a list of file system types as used with the mount command. Note that this can have negative effects on the container's security. With access to a loop device, mounting a file can circumvent the mknod permission of the devices cgroup, mounting an NFS file system can block the host's I/O completely and prevent it from rebooting, etc.

nesting.description: Allow nesting. Best used with unprivileged containers with additional id mapping. Note that this will expose procfs and sysfs contents of the host to the guest.

fuse.description: Allow using 'fuse' file systems in a container. Note that interactions between fuse and the freezer cgroup can potentially cause I/O deadlocks.
